## P1.6 - Station observations (IEM METAR)

BUILT, DEPLOYED, RUN AGAINST THE LIVE SERVICE, AND NOT SCHEDULED. Read this
before adding a Schedule Trigger.

The feed it would replace ran as a GitHub Actions cron (`7 */6 * * *`) and
arrived between 4h45m and 8h24m apart, because GitHub schedules workflows
best-effort and drops them under load. Every other weather feed - P1.2, P1.3,
P1.4, P1.5 - is already here and fresh to the hour, so moving this one looked
obvious.

IEM RATE-LIMITS BY IP, and n8n Cloud's egress is shared. Measured here on
21 Sep, three runs against the real service:

    12 concurrent   44 of 48 stations returned nothing     182 rows
     4 concurrent   42 of 48                               273 rows
     1 at a time    34 of 48                               620 rows

    every failure body: "Too many requests from your IP address, slow down."

The same 48 stations on an Actions runner take ~115 s and lose none, because
that job gets its own egress. So this workflow is correct and it is here - the
parser, the window and the guards are tested in
tests/test_observations_moved_to_n8n.py - but it runs on demand only, and
`.github/workflows/observations.yml` keeps the schedule until something proves
n8n can hold the whole board.

THE CADENCE PROBLEM IS STILL REAL AND IS A DIFFERENT PROBLEM. The fix that does
not fight the rate limit is to let n8n OWN THE TIMING and Actions own the run:
a repository_dispatch from here on a reliable schedule, which is the pattern
P2.1 - Relearn already uses. That needs a fine-grained PAT in Config, and it
does not cost an extra Actions run - the allowance is at 424 of 430.

### Writes

    weather_observations   upsert on (city_key, valid_at, source), source='IEM'
    ingest_log             via rpc/log_ingest, job='ingest_observations'

THE JOB NAME IS DELIBERATELY THE ONE THE PYTHON SCRIPT USED. PipelineStatus
reads it, and `should_run` measures the interval from
`ingest_log where job = p_job` - so a new name would have left the gate unable
to find a previous run and the cadence unenforced, while the UI showed the feed
as missing.

parameters.notes: ONE AT A TIME. IEM rate-limits by IP and answers a burst with 'Too many requests from your IP address, slow down.' - measured here at 12 concurrent (44 of 48 stations lost) and again at 4 (42 of 48). The Python job it replaces is sequential for the same reason, and the whole board takes it about 115 s, which fits this instance's 300 s cap.
